answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake tied to a verifiable on-chain history before it can trade. New identities start in a quiet lagoon of limited privileges, earning trust only through attested work, so a flood of cheap copies cannot echo the reputation of real agents. Peers then weight each agent's signal by its staked history and past attestations, making mass fake identities expensive and unprofitable while honest agents keep full access.
